# Are We Building an AI Future We Can't Power?

First listed: 2025-06-16 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Are We Building an AI Future We Can't Power?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KXk1-u2advo) - 2025-06-16
- [Substack: Are We Building an AI Future We Can't Power?](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/are-we-building-an-ai-future-we-cant-266) - 2025-06-16

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Cisco investor-relations head Sam Badri explains the move from private infrastructure to public cloud and AI, emphasizes networking opportunities and identifies electricity as a bottleneck. Cisco and NVIDIA earnings support the immediate demand observations. Eisman raises tentative concerns about Google monetization and software moats. Several simplified technical explanations are misleading, especially CPU impossibility, real-time model learning and the Blackwell Ultra rack specification; these are separated from the supported power thesis.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 001. Public cloud shifts enterprises from owning servers and switches to paying for remotely supplied compute, changing upfront capital costs into ongoing usage expenses.

- [PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02311) (2022-04-05): Authors trained 540b-parameter language model on 6,144 TPUv 4 chips. Describes next-token language modeling and model parameters, not a lookup table that simply stores all facts.
- [llama.cpp official repository](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) (current documentation inspected2026-11-10): LLM inference implementation explicitly supports x 86/ARM CPU paths and CPU/GPU hybrid use. CPU performance constraints do not make language-model inference logically impossible.

<a id="youtube-KXk1-u2advo-c008"></a>
### 008. The explanation assigns roughly 100,000 rows/columns to CPUs, billions to GPUs and trillions to TPUs as a hierarchy of model-processing capacity.

**Wrong** | Sam Badri | explanation | major

[Source at 17:12-18:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KXk1-u2advo&t=1032s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The analogy invents fixed capacity limits and confuses matrix dimensions, dataset size and parallel compute. It is not a usable quantitative explanation.

Qualification: Guest labels this a lay analogy; the broad claim that accelerators support larger practical workloads remains valid.

Conditional reasoning: A billion-by-billion matrix alone has 10^18 elements; a trillion-by-trillion matrix has 10^24. Device-class row ceilings are not architectural laws: operations can be tiled and distributed, while physical memory limits scale with hardware configuration.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

## Framework and tools

- Map the full supplier stack around a dominant chip vendor.
- Distinguish applications that raise revenue from those that reduce cost.
- Identify physical bottlenecks and distinguish orders from recognized revenue.
- Preserve uncertain moat hypotheses as hypotheses.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Cloud capex-versus-usage expense comparison
- NVIDIA69% revenue growth
- Cisco product categories and AI order target
- Rack power versus facility capacity
- Amazon/Talen 1,920MW PPA

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Cisco head of investor relations Sam Badri. Corporate product and strategy assertions are management claims, not independent industry measurements or Eisman forecasts.
- Sam Badger is Sam Badri.
- Guest repeatedly says kilowatts per hour; power should be measured in kilowatts, energy in kilowatt-hours.
- The claimed 600-700kW Blackwell Ultra figure is not silently corrected to a future architecture.
- At 2135 captions say more abundant, but immediate flat-to-down explanation indicates moribund/weak context.
- Eisman calls former Cisco leadership its founder; incidental biography not a material investment claim.
- Amazon/Talen deal today points to June 11, 2025 recording, before June 16 publication; date inference should be reconciled by root.
- Opening montage duplicates later material.
